population.text: Male patients aged 7 to 13 years with an established clinical diagnosis of DMD amenable to exon 45 skipping, on a stable dose of corticosteroids.

citations.quote: The study enrolled male patients aged 7 to 13 years, inclusive, with an established clinical diagnosis of DMD amenable to exon 45 skipping (e.g., deletions of exons such as 12-44, 18-44, 44, 46-47, 46-48, 46-49, 46-51, 46-53, or 46-55), taking a stable dose of corticosteroids for at least 24 weeks

endpoint.text: For accelerated approval: change from Baseline to Week 48 in dystrophin protein expression in biopsied muscle, as measured by western blot (a surrogate endpoint). The trial's primary clinical endpoint is change from baseline in the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) at Week 96.

result.text: Truncated dystrophin by western blot increased from 0.9% of normal at Baseline to 1.7% at Week 48 in casimersen vs 0.5% to 0.8% in placebo; mean difference 0.59%, p = 0.004. Exon 45 skipping increased with a mean difference of 1.599; p < 0.001.

citations.quote: Truncated dystrophin quantification by western blot showed a mean change in dystrophin level from 0.9% of normal at Baseline to 1.7% at Week 48 in the casimersen group, compared to a mean change from 0.5% of normal at Baseline to 0.8% of normal at Week 48 in the placebo group.
the increase in dystrophin level was statistically significantly greater in the casimersen group than in the placebo group (mean difference of 0.59%; p = 0.004)
The casimersen group had a statistically significantly greater increase in percent exon-skipping from Baseline to Week 48 than the placebo group (mean difference of 1.599; p < 0.001).

target_moa.text: Casimersen is an antisense oligonucleotide (phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer, PMO) designed to bind exon 45 of dystrophin pre-mRNA, causing exclusion of this exon during mRNA processing to restore the reading frame and produce an internally truncated but functional dystrophin protein.

citations.quote: Casimersen is an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) of the phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) subclass that was designed to target pre-messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) in the nucleus of a cell to alter the splicing process that creates a mature mRNA. Casimersen targets a region in exon 45 to restore the mRNA reading frame and induce the production of de novo truncated dystrophin protein.

Mechanism of Action	Casimersen is designed to bind to exon 45 of dystrophin pre-mRNA, resulting in exclusion of this exon during mRNA processing in patients with genetic mutations that are amenable to exon 45 skipping. Exon skipping is intended to allow for production of an internally truncated but functional dystrophin protein.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >20% and at least 5% higher than placebo): upper respiratory tract infection (65% vs 55%), cough (33% vs 26%), pyrexia (33% vs 23%), headache (32% vs 19%), arthralgia (21% vs 10%), and oropharyngeal pain (21% vs 7%). Warnings: hypersensitivity reactions (including angioedema and anaphylaxis) and potential kidney toxicity based on animal data.
